status_summary: Congress enacted 8.25 billion dollars for the Office of Science in FY2026 (Public Law 119-74, signed 2026-01-23), about level with FY2025 and about 1.16 billion above the 7.092 billion request, and did not adopt the proposed deep cut to applied energy programs, per CRS. Trade press reported on 2025-06-26 that DOE was emphasizing AI, quantum, fusion and fission at the labs, and AIP reported on 2026-04-22 that the FY2027 request seeks 7.14 billion dollars for the Office of Science, a 13 percent cut, plus 1.2 billion dollars for three AI supercomputers at Oak Ridge and Argonne funded from previously appropriated hydrogen hub money. On 2025-11-20 DOE announced a department reorganization whose new organization chart no longer lists the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, while stating that the Office of Science's core mission is unchanged, as reported by AIP FYI on 2025-11-21. On 2026-08-13 DOE announced revised national laboratory operating directives removing outdated and redundant requirements; the release does not frame the change as a refocus on basic research. No formal consolidation of the lab network was found.

timeline.event: DOE announced a department reorganization and released a new organization chart that no longer lists the Office of Clean Energy Demonstrations, the Grid Deployment Office or the Office of Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy, creating offices for fusion, for AI and quantum, and for critical minerals and energy innovation, and stating that the Office of Science's core mission is unchanged (as reported by AIP FYI).

FY2026 Energy and Water appropriations enacted as Division B of Public Law 119-74; per CRS the Office of Science received 8.250 billion dollars versus a 7.092 billion dollar request and 8.240 billion in FY2025, and the request to cut Energy Efficiency and Renewable Energy to 888 million dollars was not adopted (1.950 billion in new funding enacted).

DOE announced revisions to the operating directives for its national laboratories, plants and sites, removing outdated and redundant requirements for day-to-day field operations; the release does not name specific directives or mention basic research as a lab focus.
